## Mitigation Checklist

The following practices form the foundation of secure system design:

### 1. Principle of Least Privilege

Grant write scope (and general permissions) only to the paths and resources a process genuinely needs to function. Apply this principle at every level: users, applications, services, and processes. Deny by default, allow only what is explicitly required.

### 2. Input Validation at Trust Boundaries

Treat all external content as untrusted data, never as instructions. Establish clear trust boundaries in your system and validate every input at those boundaries. Never execute or interpret external content without first verifying its structure and intent against an allowlist of expected forms.

### 3. Path Canonicalization

Resolve and validate file paths before any write operation to block directory traversal and symlink attacks. Canonicalization removes ambiguity in path notation (e.g. `../`, `.`, symbolic links) and ensures the final resolved path lies within the intended directory scope. Reject paths that escape the allowed boundary after canonicalization.

### 4. Audit Logging

Record every denied action with its reason for later review. Logging denied operations creates an audit trail that reveals attack attempts, policy violations, and configuration errors. Include sufficient context (timestamp, actor, attempted action, reason for denial) to enable investigation and forensic analysis.
